title: Ecological corridors enhance adaptation success of translocated conflict elephants: A case study of a sub‐adult male in Hulu Terengganu, Peninsular Malaysia
content:
Human–elephant conflict (HEC) is increasing, and translocation of conflict elephants to protected areas is often the last choice. This study tracked a sub-adult male elephant translocated over 100 km, which adapted well after 90 days by spending most of its time in an ecological corridor and preferring secondary forest without any recurring conflict with humans and homing behaviour. We recommend translocating only sub-adult males to minimise future conflict.


Abstract

Human–elephant conflict (HEC), a common conflict between human and wildlife, is increasing in occurrence. To mitigate HEC, the typical final option is the translocation of conflict elephants into better-protected areas. This study tracked a sub-adult male elephant, fitted with a satellite collar, to see how it adapted to its new habitat after being translocated over 100 km away from its previous conflict zone. After 90 days, the elephant showed adaptation to its new environment. It spent 48% of its home range and 66% of its time within an ecological corridor near the translocation site. The individual preferred secondary forest, with 78.9% of its home range within secondary forest. Based on its home range, hotspots, habitat use and wildlife corridor usage, we concluded that the elephant had adapted well to its new habitat without causing conflict or exhibiting any homing behaviour. Practical implication: To enhance the success of conflict elephant translocation, we recommend relocating only sub-adult males into selected protected natural habitats to minimize the risk of future conflicts.

Abstrak

Konflik manusia–gajah (HEC) adalah antara konflik manusia-hidupan liar yang paling kerap berlaku dan meningkat setiap tahun. Untuk mengurangkan HEC, pilihan terakhir yang biasa diambil adalah dengan pemindahan gajah konflik ke kawasan yang lebih baik. Kajian ini menjejak seekor gajah jantan sub-dewasa (Kalai) yang dipasang kolar satelit untuk menilai bagaimana ia menyesuaikan diri di habitat baru selepas dipindahkan lebih 100 km dari kawasan konflik asalnya. Selepas 90 hari, Kalai menunjukkan tanda-tanda penyesuaian terhadap persekitaran baru. Gajah ini menghabiskan 48% daripada kawasan keliarannya dan 66% daripada masanya dalam koridor ekologi berhampiran tapak pemindahan. Individu ini menunjukkan pemilihan habitat yang tertinggi dalam hutan sekunder, dengan 78.9% daripada kawasan keliarannya terletak dalam hutan sekunder. Berdasarkan kawasan keliaran, kawasan titik panas, penggunaan habitat dan penggunaan koridor hidupan liar, dapat disimpulkan bahawa gajah tersebut telah menyesuaikan diri dengan baik di habitat barunya tanpa menyebabkan konflik atau menunjukkan tingkah laku kembali ke kawasan asal. Implikasi praktikal: Bagi meningkatkan kejayaan pemindahan gajah konflik, kami mengesyorkan hanya gajah jantan sub-dewasa dipindahkan ke habitat semula jadi terpilih yangdilindungi bagi mengurangkan risiko konflik pada masa hadapan.
